title: Personal Checking: extended overdraft fee and negative-balance periods by tier
content:
## Scope

When a Personal Checking account's ledger balance stays negative, three clocks run in consecutive calendar days of negative ledger balance: the extended overdraft trigger period, the restriction period and the charge-off period. This table gives each tier's extended overdraft fee and the three periods.

## Figures by tier

| Tier | Extended overdraft fee, one-time per negative episode (USD) | Extended overdraft trigger period (consecutive calendar days negative) | Restriction period (consecutive calendar days negative) | Charge-off period (consecutive calendar days negative) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Access Checking | 0.00 | 7 | 30 | 60 |
| Student Checking | 0.00 | 7 | 30 | 60 |
| Everyday Checking | 25.00 | 7 | 30 | 60 |
| Interest Checking | 25.00 | 7 | 30 | 60 |
| Premier Checking | 25.00 | 7 | 30 | 60 |
| Private Client Checking | 0.00 | 7 | 30 | 60 |

- **Extended overdraft fee**: a one-time fee per negative episode once the balance has stayed negative for the trigger period.
- **Trigger period**: consecutive calendar days of negative ledger balance after which the extended overdraft fee applies.
- **Restriction period**: consecutive calendar days of negative ledger balance after which the account is restricted.
- **Charge-off period**: consecutive calendar days of negative ledger balance after which the deficit is charged off.

## Reading the periods together (derived from the table)

The three periods are the same on every tier, so one timeline serves all six. Counted in consecutive calendar days of negative ledger balance, the trigger period of 7 days ends first, the restriction period of 30 days ends next, and the charge-off period of 60 days ends last.

**Q: Which tiers charge an extended overdraft fee?**
A: Everyday Checking, Interest Checking and Premier Checking, at 25.00 USD. Access, Student and Private Client Checking show 0.00.

**Q: Is the extended overdraft fee charged once per day the balance stays negative?**
A: No. It is a one-time fee per negative episode.
